title: Arrival Windowing — Procurement Lifecycle and Regional Hand-off Sheet
content:
Purpose:
Quick working sheet to manage staggered arrivals and SKU hand-offs across regions for the next 12 months. Focus is on minimizing cold-start capacity gaps while smoothing monthly invoice spikes and maintaining a 6-week safety window for burst events.

Summary (one-liner):
Window incoming orders into delivery lanes (three-week windows) by SKU and region, reserve a light safety buffer, and maintain a cross-region swap pool for at-risk shipments.

Key assumptions:
- Core SKUs: H100-80GB (h100-80), A100-40GB (a100-40), L40-24GB (l40-24) — names normalized for procurement tags.
- Lead-time banding based on vendor lane: factory-direct (12–20 wks), channel (8–14 wks), broker/spot (4–10 wks).
- Demand growth: +18% steady-state next 6 months, then +6% Q3->Q4.
- Target regional safety buffer: 6 weeks of peak expected burn per region (N.A., EU, APAC).
- Planned swaps allowed once per quarter per region with 2-week notice.

Notes on the table:
- Numbers are arrival *units* (racks not included); rack assembly to be scheduled based on rack-builder lead at region.
- 'primary-sku' flagged to indicate incoming dominant SKU that month to guide node provisioning templates.
- We intentionally stagger high-H100 months to avoid simultaneous invoicing spikes.

Lead-time variance mapping (lane-level):
- Factory-direct: mean 16wks, sigma 3.2wks — largest risk from factory holiday windows (Feb lunar / Dec slowdown).
- Channel partners: mean 10wks, sigma 2.0wks — fastest to reorder but limited bulk availability.
- Spot / broker: mean 6wks, sigma 4.5wks — high variance, used for fill-in only.

Risk and mitigation matrix (short):
- Risk: single-lane H100 delay (>=4 weeks) -> Mitigation: swap up to 10 units from APAC pool + activate channel tranche for NA (JIRA-OPS-1123).
- Risk: multiple small late arrivals causing <6 weeks buffer breach -> Mitigation: pre-authorize 1 emergency broker lane per region (<=30 units) and shift low-priority A100 workloads to bin-packed quiet hours.
- Risk: vendor invoice concentration -> Mitigation: spread POs across two finance cycles where possible, flag large arrivals for finance re-forecast.

Operational rules (working):
1) Window size = 3 weeks per lane; each PO assigned a target window at order time.
2) If expected arrival shifts >7 days outside window, procurement signals infra-sre + billing.
3) Cross-region swap requires: origin region approval, inbound logistics lead, and inventory reconciliation within 5 business days.
4) Rack assembly slots set weekly; assembly backlog >3 weeks triggers emergency broker lane request.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Decide on exact swap pool sizing: current recommendation = 48 units (16 per region). Approve? (@Finance, @SRE)
- Define SLA threshold for switching on emergency broker lanes (propose buffer breach <4 weeks).
- Confirm whether we want to prioritize A100 or L40 for spot fills in APAC — performance vs cost tradeoff.

Action items (owners):
- Asha P: finalize swap pool sizing proposal and run cost sim (due 2026-02-20).
- Marco L: validate assembly lead times with rack-builder partners and update monthly assembly capacity table (due 2026-02-18).
- Diane N: prepare finance split proposal for high-invoice months (due 2026-02-25).
- Kofi M: test cross-region transfer workflow in staging (inventory reconciliation scripts) and report blockers (due 2026-02-28).

Mini decision log (recent):
- 2026-01-13: Approved use of channel tranche to cover two NA H100 shortfalls (internal memo).
- 2026-02-03: Temporarily allowed broker lanes for APAC high-variance windows (trial until 2026-06).

Appendix: simple burn estimate per region (tokens = racks*cards -> capacity):
- NA peak burn: ~320 cards/week => safety buffer 6w = 1920 cards.
- EU peak burn: ~140 cards/week => safety buffer 6w = 840 cards.
- APAC peak burn: ~160 cards/week => safety buffer 6w = 960 cards.

Short notes:
- This sheet is intentionally a working artifact — expect monthly churn as new vendor quotes and lead times arrive.
- Link back to procurement playbooks in Confluence for PO templates and finance approval thresholds.

Unresolved caveat: vendor A (factory-direct) recently changed packaging spec; metric scoring of shipping damage rates pending (see slack thread linked above).
